events.text: The Burj Khalifa opens in Dubai
The Eiffel Tower is completed as the centrepiece of a world's fair in Paris
The Chrysler Building opens in New York as the tallest building in the world
The Empire State Building opens in New York

reveal.explanation: The Eiffel Tower stood as the tallest structure on Earth for forty years until the Chrysler Building's spire overtook it in 1930, and the Chrysler held the title for just eleven months before the Empire State Building opened a few streets away. Nothing since has matched that leapfrogging pace, though the Burj Khalifa of 2010 rises to more than twice the Empire State's height.

sources.excerpt: The Eiffel Tower was the world's tallest structure when completed in 1889, a distinction it retained until 1929 when the Chrysler Building in New York City was topped out.
It was both the world's first supertall skyscraper and the world's tallest building for 11 months after its completion in 1930.
The Empire State Building officially opened on May 1, 1931, forty-five days ahead of its projected opening date, and eighteen months from the start of construction.
The building was opened in 2010 as part of a new development called Downtown Dubai.

editorNotes: Alternatives checked: the Petronas Towers were dropped because their article gives conflicting years (completed 1996, world's tallest from 1998, opened 1999) and flags the tallest-building claim as disputed; the Chrysler Building replaces them. The Chrysler Building was topped out in 1929 but its article dates completion and formal opening to May 1930, which is used. The Empire State Building was structurally complete on 11 April 1931 and opened on 1 May 1931, the same year. The Eiffel Tower's structural work finished in March 1889 and it opened to the public in May 1889. The Burj Khalifa was topped out in 2009 and officially opened on 4 January 2010; the opening is the event used.
